moat_source: installed-base services and hyperscaler qualification cycles in power/cooling; evidence: 252% order growth and pricing power (+170bps margin) - but Schneider/Eaton compete for every large award and the product is ultimately engineered equipment, not a standard

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% closed by year 3.

sensitivity_key_driver: order normalization slope (when 252% growth mean-reverts and to what level)
primary_model_risk: Bullwhip: 252% order growth during capacity shortages includes double-ordering and safety-stock building. The $15B backlog de-risks 2026-27 revenue but says nothing about 2028 orders. Base case assumes orders normalize to trend without contraction; the bear case (orders contract as hyperscaler capex digests) is the standard outcome after order booms of this magnitude in electrical equipment.
expectations_gap_key_variable: order-book permanence: at ~44x forward earnings the market extrapolates the 252% order surge; our base case converts the backlog fully and still lands ~31% below the price because the terminal year cannot sustain boom-era order rates
top_5_bull_arguments: $15B backlog is contracted revenue - 2026-27 numbers are essentially locked
252% order growth with margin expansion shows pricing power, not just volume
Liquid cooling is a genuine new product cycle layered on the power franchise
AMZN ($200B) and MSFT (~$190B) capex plans flow directly into Vertiv's addressable spend
Bull case ($392) exceeds the price if the build-out runs uninterrupted through 2030
top_5_bear_arguments: Expected IV ($229.50) is ~31% below the price; ~44x forward for cyclical equipment is a cycle-peak multiple
Order booms of this scale in electrical equipment have always included double-ordering that unwinds
Schneider and Eaton have larger service networks and balance sheets for the retrofit war
Same single-factor exposure (hyperscaler capex) as the entire AI complex - no diversification benefit
Sourced order/backlog data is from February; a July analysis on February order data in a fast cycle deserves a reliability haircut (scored 7)
thesis_breakers: Book-to-bill below 1.0 in any quarter (normalization arriving)
A major hyperscaler standardizing on Schneider/Eaton for liquid cooling
Adjusted operating margin contracting y/y (pricing power gone)
position_size_recommendation: 0% at current price; the backlog makes it safer than its multiple suggests near-term, but entry only makes sense near expected IV (~$230) after the first order-normalization scare
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROE/ROA null: not captured as sourced ratios. Reliability 7 (not 8): the order/backlog/margin data is February-2026 vintage - the freshest quarter was not captured in research; forward EPS implied from the quoted forward P/E. FCF path constructed from forward earnings - confidence_level medium.
historical_context: Directional context only - low confidence. Verified datapoints: +145.25% over 52 weeks, -4.8% over two weeks vs SPY +2.7% (barchart/chartmill via search), trailing P/E 75.53 / forward 44.02, analyst target 376.96 (pass1). No verified historical multiple range captured.
